cards.design_implication: If single-molecule biomechanical parameters like Young's modulus are the research targets, experimental designs should consider integrating AFM or OT capabilities rather than relying solely on bulk techniques.
does_not_establish: Quantitative accuracy or precision limits of AFM/OT for specific materials.
Protocol details for calibrating AFM or OT instruments.
Comparative performance metrics against specific bulk techniques under identical conditions.
cards.evidence_excerpt: In this framework, atomic force microscopy (AFM) and optical tweezers (OT) can play an important role to determine the biomechanical parameters of the investigated systems at the single-molecule level. This review aims to fully comprehend the interplay between mechanical forces and soft matter systems. In particular, we outline the capabilities of AFM and OT compared to other classical bulk techniques to determine nanomechanical parameters such as Young's modulus.
limitations: The statement is derived from a review abstract summarizing the capabilities of the methods.
Specific experimental conditions, sample preparations, or validation data for these measurements are not provided.
cards.statement: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) and optical tweezers (OT) are used to determine biomechanical parameters, such as Young's modulus, at the single-molecule level in soft matter systems.

cards.design_implication: When designing studies involving cellular systems, investigators might consider incorporating biomechanical stimuli to probe the role of transduction processes in health or disease models.
does_not_establish: Specific molecular pathways linking biomechanical action to transduction.
The magnitude or threshold of mechanical force required to elicit a response.
Causal conclusions applicable to specific disease states without further evidence.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Moreover, cellular transduction processes which are involved in health and disease conditions are significantly affected by exogenous biomechanical actions.
limitations: The abstract provides a general statement without specifying the exact biological mechanisms or pathways involved.
No primary experimental data is cited in this abstract to support the causal link.
cards.statement: Exogenous biomechanical actions significantly affect cellular transduction processes involved in health and disease conditions.
